name: Genetic Vascular Anomaly

criteria.description: Presence of a first-degree relative with a confirmed genetic vascular anomaly
Identification of a vascular malformation on clinical examination or imaging
Detection of pathogenic variant in a gene known to cause vascular anomalies
Presence of characteristic cutaneous vascular lesions such as port-wine stains or telangiectasias
Congenital or early childhood onset of vascular anomaly symptoms

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: At least two major criteria including family history and vascular malformation, or one major criterion plus genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is recommended but not mandatory if clinical criteria are met.

searchTerms: flat red skin patches present at birth

pathognomonic.symptomName: Genetically confirmed pathogenic variant in vascular anomaly gene
searchTerms: confirmed gene mutation causing blood vessel issues

common.symptomName: Telangiectasias on skin or mucous membranes
searchTerms: small visible blood vessels on skin or mouth

common.symptomName: Localized soft tissue swelling due to venous malformations
searchTerms: soft tissue lumps due to vein malformations

common.symptomName: Recurrent spontaneous bleeding from vascular lesions
searchTerms: repeated bleeding from blood vessel lesions
pain caused by blood vessel abnormalities
one limb larger than the other

occasional.symptomName: Neurological symptoms secondary to vascular malformations (e.g. seizures)
searchTerms: seizures caused by blood vessel problems
brain symptoms linked to vessel abnormalities

occasional.symptomName: Cardiovascular complications such as high-output cardiac failure
searchTerms: heart problems from high blood flow
heart failure due to vascular issues
cardiac complications from blood vessel malformations
skin sores over blood vessel growths
open wounds on abnormal blood vessels
lung blood vessel malformations causing low oxygen
lung vascular anomalies causing oxygen deficiency
bleeding in digestive tract from vascular lesions
GI bleeding due to blood vessel malformations

rare.symptomName: Renal vascular anomalies leading to hypertension
searchTerms: kidney blood vessel problems causing high blood pressure

laboratory: Elevated D-dimer levels in cases with extensive venous malformations
Normal coagulation profile unless complicated by bleeding
imaging: MRI or ultrasound demonstrating characteristic vascular malformations
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes such as RASA1, TEK, or ENG
other: Histopathology showing abnormal vascular channels with thin walls

redFlags: Rapid enlargement of vascular lesion with pain or ulceration
Neurological deficits suggestive of cerebral vascular involvement
references: Blei F, et al. Vascular anomalies: classification, diagnosis, and management. J Vasc Surg. 2020.
